source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A dying client's feet are cold and mottled. Which change does this reflect?
questions.rationale: Slowing circulation causes mottling, cyanosis, and cold skin starting at the feet, with a weaker pulse and lower BP.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Signs of Impending Death (PDF p. 53)
questions.quote: Mottling and cyanosis of the extremities

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Noisy breathing from mucus in the throat of a dying client is called:
questions.rationale: The death rattle is noisy breathing from mucus collecting in the throat.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Signs of Impending Death (PDF p. 53)
questions.quote: Noisy breathing, referred to as the death rattle

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: How can the nurse help a dying client keep a sense of control?
questions.rationale: Supporting control includes letting clients choose the location and timing of care and activities.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Care of the Dying (PDF p. 53)
questions.quote: allow clients to choose the location of care times of appointm

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Why should the nurse repeat information to the family of a dying client?
questions.rationale: The family may not absorb information because of stress and grieving, so it is repeated.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Supporting the Family (PDF p. 54)
questions.quote: Repeat the provided information because they may not absorb it due to stress and grieving

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Stiffening of the body about 2 to 4 hours after death is:
questions.rationale: Rigor mortis results from lack of ATP and begins about 2–4 hours after death.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Postmortem Care (PDF p. 54)
questions.quote: Stiffening of the body that occurs about 2 to 4 hours after death

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: How fast does body temperature fall after death (algor mortis)?
questions.rationale: Body temperature falls about 1°C (1.8°F) per hour until room temperature.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Postmortem Care (PDF p. 54)
questions.quote: Body temperature falls about 1°C (1.8°F) per hour until it reaches room temperature

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Why is a pillow placed under the head after death?
questions.rationale: A pillow under the head and shoulders prevents facial discoloration from settling blood (livor mortis).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Postmortem Care (PDF p. 54)
questions.quote: One pillow is placed under the head and shoulders to prevent blood from discoloring the face

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: During postmortem care, what is done with dentures?
options: Inserted to give a natural look
questions.rationale: Dentures are usually inserted to give the face a natural appearance, and the mouth is closed.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Postmortem Care (PDF p. 54)
questions.quote: Dentures are usually inserted to help give the face a natural appearance

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Before a CT scan with contrast, which lab results should be checked?
questions.rationale: Kidney function (BUN, creatinine) is checked because contrast is excreted by the kidneys.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, CT Scan (PDF p. 55)
questions.quote: Check BUN & Creatinine

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After a contrast CT, what should the client do?
questions.rationale: Increased fluids help eliminate the contrast medium; watch for delayed allergic reactions.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, CT Scan (PDF p. 55)
questions.quote: Increase fluid intake to help eliminate the contrast medium

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: For which client is an MRI contraindicated?
options: Client with a cast of plaster
questions.rationale: MRI is contraindicated with metal in the body and pacemakers.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, MRI (PDF p. 56)
questions.quote: Patients with pacemakers

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What should the client expect during an MRI?
questions.rationale: MRI is painless but noisy, with loud banging; the client must stay still.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, MRI (PDF p. 56)
questions.quote: Tell the client to expect to hear loud banging from the scanner

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After a PET scan, what should the client do with urine?
questions.rationale: Flush immediately after each voiding; increase fluids for 24–48 hours.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, PET Scan (PDF p. 56)
questions.quote: Flush the toilet immediately after each voiding

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should a client prepare hair for an EEG?
options: Wash it; no sprays or creams
questions.rationale: Hair should be clean, without sprays, creams, or oils, which impair electrode contact.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, EEG (PDF p. 57)
questions.quote: Instruct the client to clean the hair and refrain from using hair sprays, creams of solutions

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How long before an EEG should caffeine be avoided?
questions.rationale: Avoid caffeine-containing beverages for 8 hours before the EEG.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, EEG (PDF p. 57)
questions.quote: Refrain from drinking caffeine-containing beverages for 8 hours before the procedure

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client fears the EEG will shock him. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: The EEG records brain activity and does not cause electric shock.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, EEG (PDF p. 57)
questions.quote: Inform the client that EEG does not cause electric shock.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How is a client positioned for lumbar puncture?
questions.rationale: The C-shaped, fetal, or knee-chest position widens the space between lumbar vertebrae (L3–L4 or L4–L5).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Lumbar Puncture (PDF p. 58)
questions.quote: Position: Knee-chest position / C-shaped position I Fetal position I Shrimp

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which CSF finding suggests bacterial meningitis?
questions.rationale: Bacterial and TB meningitis decrease CSF glucose and increase protein and lactic acid.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Lumbar Puncture (PDF p. 58)
questions.quote: Glucose - Bacterial and Tubercular Meningitis

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When is lumbar puncture contraindicated?
questions.rationale: LP is contraindicated with infection at the site and coagulation defects, and used cautiously with increased ICP.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Lumbar Puncture (PDF p. 58)
questions.quote: This procedure is contraindicated if infection is present at the needle insertion site

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After a lumbar puncture, what helps replace lost CSF?
questions.rationale: If permitted, fluids are given to replace lost CSF; the site is watched for leakage.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Lumbar Puncture (PDF p. 58)
questions.quote: If permitted, administer fluids to replace lost CSF

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What sensation should a client expect during EMG needle insertion?
questions.rationale: Clients feel a sensation like an intramuscular injection as the needle enters the muscle.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, EMG (PDF p. 60)
questions.quote: expect sensation similar to that of an intramuscular injection

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which is a contraindication to EMG?
questions.rationale: EMG is contraindicated with extensive skin infection, anticoagulant therapy, and infection at electrode sites.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, EMG (PDF p. 60)
questions.quote: Anticoagulant therapy
